of increasing the number of PHCs operating  24x7 as well as upgradation of PHCs/ 
CHCs to FRUs with all the States/ UTs so that a critical service like Health Care is 
available to the targeted beneficiaries wherever required.                            (Para 4.6)

The success of Family Welfare Programme depends to a large extent, upon the

various level is imparted through the network of Training Centres and Schools. Approved 
outlay of Rs. 669.58 crore has been kept under Eleventh Plan for grants to State Training 
Institutions. The Committee notes that out of this allocation, major funding of Rs. 
520.48 crore is meant for basic training for ANMs/ LHVs and Rs. 56.09 crore for 
basic training for MPWs (Male). The Comm ittee notes that out of Rs. 520.48 crore 
kept for training of ANMs/ LHVs, only Rs . 218.04 crore have been released during 
the first three years of the Eleventh Plan. With Rs. 85.18 crore proposed for 2010-
11, more than Rs. 200.00 crore would be left for the last year of the plan period. Not 
only this, during 2008-09 and 2009-10, the allocated funds have remained under-
utilised. The Committee finds that funds meant for basic training for MPWs (Male) 
also could not be put to optimum use during the Eleventh Plan period so far.                  
(Para 4.13) 
 
4.14 While trying to analyse the reasons for such a state of affairs under the most 
crucial component i.e., training of key functionaries positioned at Sub-Centres and PHCs, 
the Committee finds that limited capacity of ANM schools poses problems in availability 
of ANMs. In other words, the lack of training school for ANMs is also indirectly 
responsible for shortage of ANMs. The Committee was given to understand that States 
have the option to use NRHM resources to restart/ open new ANM training schools. The 
Committee also notes that Lady Health Visitors, a promotional post for ANMs, are 
required to undergo 6 months training in LHV training schools. However, due to LHV 
training schools being closed down in many States, required training was not being 
imparted to LHVs. Situation is more grim w ith respect to training of MPWs (Male) as 
States have simply stopped recruitment of MPWs (Male) for many years due to closing 
down of training schools. The Committee is not aware about the reasons for lack of 
interest on the part of State Government s for creating/ strengthening the training 
schools meant for key Health functionaries with the support of Central Funds. The 
Committee strongly feels that it is high  time for the Department to make an 
assessment of this crucial area in consultation with all the States/ UTs and bring 

 187
about all round improvement. One must not forget that a fully trained and qualified 
health worker alone can handle his job responsibilities effectively.       
(Para 4.14)

a  thorough review of strategies. The low utilization of funds has seriously hampered

concerned with this state of affair s, the Committee recommends that the

 The Committee is constrained to observe that this is yet another case of inept 
handling of budgeted funds by the Department. The Committee finds to its dismay

From a perusal of the information made available, the Committee would like 
to state here that significant progress un der the Immunisation Programme has not 
been noticed in many of the States. This fa ct holds true both for the high focus and

Nadu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, the immu nization coverage has infact dropped

of the very densely populated States like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh means that a very

execution of the plans are made by the programme authorities, visible impact on the 

 191
immunization coverage would remain a distant dream. It, therefore, urges the

Cold chain maintenance is the most  crucial component for effective 
implementation of the Immunisation  Programme. The Committee, however, 
observes that so far this has proved to be the weakest link under the programme.

maintenance arrangement made under the Performance Audit of CAG. As per the

MALARIA 
 
The Committee notes that the number of cases reported is already on the rise 
in many of the States, especially the No rth-Eastern States, where the problem is 
acute. Under the GFATM project all the 77 district in 7 NE States, 7 districts of 
Jharkhand, 6 districts of West Bengal and 16  districts of Orissa are covered.  The 
Committee is not fully convinced by the Departments, contention that due to remote 
and inaccessible areas with poor access to malaria diagnosis and treatment facilities, 
NE states continue to remain a major cha llenge.  The Committee would like to state 
here that the programme has been these for considerable period and with 100 
percent central funding and also Internatio nal assistance, these challenges, should 
have been significantly lessened. The Comm ittee also finds that major interventions 
like introduction of Rapid diagnostic kits , for the field workers, introduction of 
specialized therapy for Pf cases and long lasting insecticidal nets have all been made 
for North East States.  However, inspite of such huge funding under the programme 
significant progress is not visible. The Committee can only conclude that 
supervision and monitoring, which is one of the main strategies adopted for effective 
control of malaria, is perhaps not being implemented to the desired levels, especially 
in NE region and Orissa.                                  (Para 6.7) 
 
The Committee would however, like to draw the attention of the Department 
to the status of some key functionaries under Malaria control programme. The 
Committee is astonished to find that inspit e of special attention being given to the 
NE States important functionaries are simply not there as indicated below: 
- Vector borne Disease Control (DVBOC) Consultant is not there in any of 
the                 NE States and Sikkim.  

 195
- Only 522 PHC-MOs are posted in Arunachal Pradesh. Remaining States 
do not have this functionary. 
- Assam does not have a Lab-Technician/ Lab-Technician(Contractual)  
- Both Assam and Nagaland do not have a Health Supervisor (M) 
- No Health Supervisor (F) is post ed in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, 
Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. 
- Multi-Purpose Worker (M) is not there in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. 
- Only Nagaland has 28 Malaria Inspectors 
- Surveillance Staff (307) is there only in Meghalaya.

- In Sikkim and Tripura Malaria Tec hnical Supervisors (Contractual) are 
not  there  
- n Arunachal Pradesh and Assam there are no regular MPW (M) at all  
(Para 6.9) 
 
 The fact that these functionaries play a vital role in disease detection and 
surveillance cannot be set aside. By not appointing these functionaries, the States 
leave a large gap in the field-level disease surveillance and treatment. The 
Committee can only conclude from the above that it would be impractical to expect 
noticeable improvements in malaria control with key functionaries missing, that too, 
in the malaria endemic States.   Hence, the Committee advises the Department that, 
apart from allocating sufficient funds to these States/ UTs, it should also pursue

per pair of eyes towards honorarium of Eye  Banks Staff, appointment of Eye 
donation Counsellors have also seemed to have made no impact.        
(Para 9.12)                         
 
 The Committee has been given to understand that it is normal that all cornea 
collected cannot be used for replantation purpose, as it needs to be assessed by 
cornea specialist for suitability and quality of cornea.  Only 30 to 40 percent corneas 
collected are suitable for optical Keratopl asty.  The Committee would like to point 
out that as per the above st ate-specific details, percentage of corneas utilized is 
much below the accepted 30 to 40 percent level.  One obvious reason for such a low 
level of utilization can be the upkeep and maintenance of Eye Banks being not as 
per the standard norms. The Committee , therefore, recommends to the Department 
to keep the activities of all the entities/institutions  involved in providing eye 
collection activities under constant scruti ny/monitoring and take urgent remedial 
steps so that the stumbling blocks in the optimum utilization of eyes collected is 
achieved by more number of beneficiaries getting back their vision.                          
 The Committee would like to know as to whether the Government is aware 
of the work done by Dr. Sinha.                                   (Para 9.13) 
 
X. NATIONAL IODINE DEFICIENCY DISORDERS CONTROL 
PROGRAMME 
 
 
 The Committee is not very happy with  the trends of fund utilization under 
the programme. During 2007-08 and 2008-09 against an allocation of Rs. 25.00 crore 
and Rs. 32.00 crore respectively, expenditur e reported is only Rs. 19.45 crore and 
Rs. 17.95 crore respectively.  The Committee observes that every year there have 
been substantial amount of savings over the allocated funds. The Committee notes 
with disappointment that this neither speaks of good financial management nor 

 204
good programme implementation under the Programme. The Committee once 
again recommends to the Department to devi se measures to overcome the obstacles 
coming in the way of proper implementation of the programme initiatives.   
(Para 10.3)                                  
 
The Committee hopes that the Empowered Programme Committee (EPC) 
approval must have been received by now and also the biding process on the 
technical specifications of salt testin g kits, must have been completed. The 
Committee would like to emphasise that all conceivable efforts may be made so as to 
ensure optimal and judicious allocation of funds in active coordination with state 
authority for timely achievements of the targets during  2010-11.       (Para 10.4) 
 
 The Committee understands from the above  that as many as nine States/ UTs 
have been highly endemic iodine deficien cy. The Committee, however, does not find 
that any focused intervention has been initiated in the above States/ UTs to reduce 
the deficiency rate. Since, the above ob servation is a result of certain sample 
districts surveyed in the above States/ UTs the numbers would be much more if all 
the districts in these States/ UTs are co vered. Therefore, the Committee suggests 
that a special intervention needs to be made in all of the above States/UTs.  
Intensified IEC activities may also be carr ied out covering all the districts so that 
the prevalence rate comes to less than 10. The Committee would like the 
Department to furnish details of the samp le survey report concerning all the States/ 
UTs covered for its perusal.                             (Para 10.6) 
 
XI INTEGRATED DISEASE SURVEILLANCE PROGRAMME 
 The Committee fails to understand as to why clear information has not been 
furnished by the Ministry against the targ ets set by it for 2009-10. The Committee 
observes that concrete data is necessary for proper assessment of the targets set and 
merely stating that  training programme is in progress or connectivity on Broad 
Band is being established without quantify ing the progress made evinces ignorance 
of the most basic principles of appraisa l on the part of the Department.  The 
Committee would like the Department to furnish details of achievement during 
2009-10 regarding the targets mentioned above in the table for 2009-10 while 

 205
furnishing its ATN and also be more circumspect while furnishing the information 
in the Outcome Budget.                         (Para 11.3) 
 
 
 The Committee is happy to note that  the recruitment and training of the 
required manpower under IDSP is proceeding at a positive pace. The Committee 
observes that the presence of trained surveillance manpower are key to the 
prevention and control of diseases/ epidem ic in such a large country as India. 
Hence, the Committee hopes that the targ ets of recruiting and training technical 
consultants for the remaining 400 vacant post would have been completed after 
due approval for restructuring and extension of IDSP were obtained. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends the Departme nt to furnish the details in this 
regard for its perusal. The Committee wo uld also like to be apprised of the 
progress made towards establishing video conferencing at the remaining sites and 
strengthening the remaining priority labs.                           (Para 11.5)

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE GOVERNMENT
IV.    SAFDARJUNG HOSPITAL
Recommendations/Observations
4.5    The Committee observes that whereas Non-Plan funds for the hospital allocated in the first two years of Tenth
Plan could be utilized fully, plan allocation remained underutilized. In view of the higher allocation of plan funds in
2004-05 (from Rs. 45.00 crore in 2003-04 to Rs. 60.00 crores in 2004-05), the Department should take all the required
steps for its optimum and judicious utilisation.
Action Taken
         The major reason for under utilization of the plan funds for 2002-03 and 2003-04 was due to savings under the
sub-head Machinery and Equipment. This was due to the fact that the debits against the Letter of Credits were opened
for procurement of imported Machinery and Equipments; but debits against the LOCs could not be received during the
same financial year from foreign suppliers. Funds also remained unutilized due to non-completion of various codal
formalities regarding procurement.
         There is higher allocation of funds in 2004-05 i.e. Rs. 60 crores against Rs.45 crores in 2003-04. The Additional
funds are provided to meet the normal increase in expenditure annually and to procure the major equipment including
the equipments like M.R.I., Spiral C.T. Scan for which action for procurement was initiated during 2003-04. The
expenditure involved in procurement of these equipments and Brachytherapy is to the tune of Rs. 13.24 crores (approx.).
The procurement of these equipments is at an advanced stage.
         The pattern of expenditure is reviewed periodically in the Ministry to ensure that funds are utilized fully.
V.     RAM MANOHAR LOHIA HOSPITAL, NEW DELHI
Recommendations/Observations
5.1    The Plan allocation for this hospital in BE 2003-04 was Rs. 19.00 crores which has been marginally increased to
Rs. 22.00 crores in BE 2004-05. In respect of setting up of a Post Graduate Institute at RML hospital, the Department
has informed that the total Tenth Plan allocation for Dr. RML Hospital is Rs. 150.00 crores which also includes the cost
of establishment of Post Graduate Institute at Dr. RML. Hospital. An EFC for establishment of Post Graduate Institute
at Dr. RML Hospital has already been approved. However, the construction work for the Institute is yet to be started. An
outlay of Rs. 8.00 crores has been made for construction works under capital head for the Hospital during this financial
year i.e. 2004-05. Besides, a provision of Rs. 50.00 lakhs as token amount for the Institute has also been kept in the Plan
budget of the Hospital.
Recommendations/Observations
5.2    The Committee is anguished to note that during the first two years of the Tenth Plan, nothing beyond obtaining
EFC approval for the Post Graduate Institute could be achieved. The construction work is yet to start. The Committee
feels that at this sluggish pace, the proposed teaching institute may not be established during the Tenth Plan. The
Committee feels that a time bound Action Plan for completion of this Project must have been chalked out by the
Department in consultation with the hospital authorities. The Committee strongly feels that the Department should
strictly adhere to this Action Plan so that the proposed Dental Institute is established at the earliest. If setting up of this
PG institute requires more funds, the Committee recommends that the Department may provide the same.
Action Taken
         The foundation stone for the Post Graduate Courses at Dr. RML Hospital has been laid by the Hon’ble Union
Health Minister on 25
th November, 2004. Land has already been acquired and an allocation of Rs.30 crores have been
proposed under the Plan Head (for the year 2005-06) for construction of building of PGIMER. Initiative has been
undertaken to complete the construction work of the PGIMER in a time bound manner. Necessary steps are also being
taken to ensure that the required manpower for teaching is available to run the PG Courses at the Institute so that the
Institute starts functioning at the earliest.
VI.    ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES (AIIMS), NEW DELHI
Recommendations/Observations
6.6    The Committee notes that last year a Scheme called Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana was formulated
wherein it was decided in principle to set up one AIIMS type institution each in the States of Bihar (Patna), Chhattisgarh

(Raipur), Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal), Orissa (Bhubaneshwar), Rajasthan (Jodhpur) and Uttaranchal (Rishikesh). Under
this Scheme, it is also proposed to upgrade one medical college each in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, J&K,
Tamil Nadu, UP and West Bengal to the level of proposed AIIMS like institutions. The Committee observes that these
States were chosen as they were underserved in terms of medical infrastructure, high incidence of mortality and
morbidity etc.
Action Taken
         The proposal to set up six AIIMS like institutions and upgradation of 7 medical colleges under the Pradhan Mantri
Swasthya Suraksha Yojana has been considered by the Expenditure Finance Committee on 24.11.2004 and will now be
placed before the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs for clearance. Pending these clearances, start-up activities
like construction of boundary wall, the process for selection of Project Consultant for providing comprehensive
consultancy services and selection of architectural concepts/designs for AIIMS like institution have been taken up.
Recommendations/Observations
6.7    The Committee notes that against a provision of Rs. 6 crores for the project in 2003-04, Rs. 60 crores have been
provided during 2004-05. The Committee would like to point out that the estimated cost for the project is Rs. 4158 crore
with Rs. 280 crore being the expenditure on each new AIIMS and recurring expenditure of Rs. 60 crore to be borne by
the Central Government annually. The Committee expresses its extreme dissatisfaction with the pace of progress made
in the project so far specially in the light of wide publicity given to the project. The Committee finds that only in
principle approval by the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance has been accorded so far. The Scheme is
currently in the process of being placed before the Expenditure Finance Committee. The Committee would like to
emphasise that all the procedural formalities should be completed at the earliest. The Committee is also surprised to note
that only Rs. 60 crores have been provided for this project during 2004-05. The Committee is of the view that this
project should be completed within the time limit of 3 years and necessary funds should be provided at the RE stage
during the current year itself.
Action Taken
         The tentative cost of setting up each institute comes around Rs. 284.50 crores and annual estimated recurring cost
on salaries, maintenance etc., comes to Rs. 60 crores per institute. Rs.6 crores have been released for boundary wall
construction. During the year Rs. 60 crores were provided for the scheme in the Budget. However, at RE stage the
provision has been reduced to Rs. 10 crores due to delay in Project Clearance. Sufficient budget provision will be kept
for the financial year 2005-06 after receipt of Plan budget from the Planning Commission.

         There has been a declining trend of malaria cases as well as deaths in these states, however, Plasmodium
falciparum malaria is still a cause of concern in states like Tripura, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Manipur and Assam where the
proportion of Plasmodium falciparum cases varies between 45 to 78 per cent which is the main cause of complicated
and severe malaria resulting in deaths. Resistance to anti malarial drug Chloroquine is also an emerging problem in
these states.
         Government of India provides 100 per cent cash assistance in these States to meet out operational cost of the
programme in addition to supply of anti malarial drugs, anti filaria drug, insecticides and larvicides.
         In view of the difficult terrain and remote and inaccessible areas, Government of India has included North Eastern
States excluding Sikkim for additional support from Global Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. The State of
Orissa has 30 districts out of which half the districts contribute 80 per cent of total malaria, Plasmodium Falciparum
cases and deaths in the state. Some areas in Keonjhar, Kaandhamal and Sundergarh districts have also reported drug
resistance to anti malarial drug, Chloroquine. In these areas Government is providing alternative drugs for the treatment
of Plasmodium Falciparum malaria cases. There is also problem of vector resistance to insecticide DDT and Malathion
in some districts. Government of India is providing additional support to the State of Orissa under World Bank assisted
Enhanced Malaria Control Project (EMCP) in addition to the supply of anti malarial drugs, anti-filaria drugs,
insecticides and larvicides. Government has also included some districts of the State for additional support from Global
Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.
         The State of West Bengal has 32 districts, out of which six districts are mainly malaria affected. These six districts
contribute 60 to 70 per cent of total malaria cases, 90 per cent of Plasmodium Falciparum cases and 85 per cent of
malaria deaths in the State. There are also pockets of drug resistance to anti malarial drug Chloroquine in these districts.
In view of the high incidence of malaria in these districts, Government of India have included these districts for
additional support under the Global Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.

The Committee is left with no other alternative but to conclude that funds under this programme are not being utilized in

Action Taken
         Government of India provides assistance to States for implementation of National Vector Borne Disease Control
Programme in the following manner:
            1.    All States in the country are provided commodity grants in the form of supply of drugs for treatment of
malaria, filaria and Kalazar, larvicides, insecticides, as per the technical requirements of States. Cash grants
is provided only for activities related to training, information and for education, information and
communication for Malaria and observance of Mass Drug Administration Programme of
Doethylcarbamazine (DEC) tablets to achieve elimination of Lymphatic Filariasis and implementation of
computerized Management Information System.
            2.    In the World Bank assisted Enhanced Malaria Control Project-Government of India provides 100 per cent
cash assistance for meeting the operational cost of the programme in 8 high malaria endemic States namely
Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Orissa.
            3.    For North-Eastern States Government of India is providing 100 per cent cash assistance to NE States to
meet the operational cost of the programme.
            4.    Government of India allocates funds to States as per approved annual action plan within annual outlay for
National Vector Borne Diseases Control Programme. However, during the year some States demanded for
more drugs and insecticides due to unforeseen situation of the vector borne diseases and thus they are
allocated additional quantities of the items over and above the initial allocation as per annual action plan. On
account of this, the expenditure shown by some states is on higher side.
            5.    In the States/UTs of Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry and Delhi the supply of anti malarial drugs could not be
effected in the year 2002-03 and 2003-04 to which the expenditure was less in the States.
            6.    The programme is being monitored regularly in order to ensure judicious use of funds and commodities
made available to the programme through statement of expenditure and utilization certificates submitted by
States.
Recommendations/Observations
8.7    1045 PHCs predominantly inhabited by tribals in 120 districts in eight States of Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh,
Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Orissa and Rajasthan are also being provided additional support
including operational expenses under Enhanced Malaria Control Project (EMCO) with World Bank assistance. World
Bank mission which reviewed the project in January, 2004, has noted that 30 per cent reduction in the morbidity has
been recorded against the project goal of 10 per cent. The Committee feels that the ground realities in the remaining
districts of these States as well as other endemic States being run on domestic funding are not good. Number of cases of
reported deaths reveal the clear picture.

While appreciating the achievement level in the 120 districts of Right States covered by EMCP with World Bank
assistance, the Committee is of the view that the Department may get an assessment done of these districts to ascertain

the special measures initiated there. The Committee feels that adoption of similar strategy in other districts not covered
by World Bank assistance may result in better achievement level there also.
Action Taken
         The Directorate of NVBDCP is continuously monitoring malaria situation in the country. It is a fact that under the
World Bank assisted project (EMCP) in eight States namely Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh,
Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, and Orissa there has been a decline in the Malaria incidence in most of the
districts.
         Monitoring of the programme in other States indicates that due to shortage of the health care workers, the
surveillance of malaria is not up to the mark in some states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Uttaranchal). While in States like Goa
and Karnataka, the incidence of the malaria as well as Plasmodium Falciparum (cerebral malaria) is showing an
increasing trend.
         Considering these facts 26 districts in the five States are also being proposed under the Enhanced Vector Borne
Diseases Control Project (EVBDCP) for additional support for a period of five years.
         The strategy for control of malaria in the country is similar for all States which includes Early Diagnosis and
Prompt Treatment of malaria cases, Integrated Vector Control Management, Inter-sectoral Collaboration, Information
Education, Communication and Motivation, Capacity Building and monitoring and evaluation, including Computerized
Management Information System.
X.     KALA-AZAR CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
10.4  The Committee feels that with the number of deaths being reported every year the target of elimination of
Kalaazar in National Health Policy may not be achieved. The Committee therefore, is of the view that there is need of
constant monitoring by the Department and follow up by taking corrective measures.
Action Taken
         Regular monitoring as suggested by the Committee is being done and States are being persuaded to take corrective
measures to gear up anti Kala-Azar activities.
XI.    TUBERCULOSIS CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
11.2  The Committee notes that the plan allocation of Rs. 108 crores in 2003-04 has been enhanced to Rs. 115 crores in
2004-05. As per the State-wise figures available with the Committee, position regarding fund allocation/release and
utilisation thereof during 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2003-04 does not reveal a satisfactory performance. In 2001-02, against
an allocation of Rs. 133.00 crore, only Rs. 102.88 crore could be utilized. During 2002-03, against an allocation of Rs.
107.00 crore, utilisation figures are Rs. 87.46 crore. However, during 2003-04, utilisation figures (Rs. 113.09 crore)
exceed the funds allocated (Rs. 107.60 crore). The Committee observes that overall details do not reveal the factual
position about the performance of individual States. Expenditure in a large number of states exceeds the allocated funds;
there are some states that could not fully utilize the allocated funds. The Committee fails to comprehend the real
problem areas being indicated in this programme. Whereas there are some States, which failed to utilize the allocated
funds, there are States which exceeded the allocated funds. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that the Department
should pursue the matter of proper utilisation of funds as per the prescribed norms/Guidelines with the concerned State
Governments.
Action Taken
         Under the National TB Control Programme, initial allocation of funds to the States is made in the beginning of the
financial year tentatively on the pro-rata basis of population of the respective States. However, the expenditure of the
States depends on their actual requirement of cash grant and commodity assistance. The cash grant depends on the trend

XIII.NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR CONTROL OF BLINDNESS (NPCB)
Recommendations/Observations
13.6  The Committee is surprised to note that in spite of so many initiatives taken by the Government and sufficient
funds also being there, Bihar and Assam continue to be the lowest performing States and have cataract surgery rate of
less than 200 operations/lakh population, against the targets of the Tenth Plan to increase the cataract surgery rate to 450
operations per lakh population. The Committee observes that Bihar has simply failed to utilize the allocated funds.
Against an allocation of 1.57 crores in
2002-03, expenditure incurred was only Rs. 57 lakhs. Similarly, for 2003-04 provisional expenditure reported is Rs. 39
lakhs against an allocation of Rs. 2.5 crores.
Action Taken
         Reasons for sub-optimal performance in Bihar and Assam include the following:----
              (1)   Inadequate infrastructure and human resources for providing eye care services.
              (2)   Limited eye care facilities in voluntary sector.
         Adequate funds were released to these states for improvement in service. There has not been much improvement
in expenditure in these States. Sector specific review to analyze the factors responsible for non-utilization is being
undertaken so that funds earmarked may be optimally utilized in future.
Recommendations/Observations
13.7 The Committee notes that as per the National Survey 2001-02, prevalence of blindness was estimated to be 1.38
per cent in N E States as compared of the National average of 1.1 per cent. Eye-care infrastructure is weak in N E
region, number of Eye Surgeons are also inadequate. Very few NGOs are located in the region. The Committee strongly
feels that there is a need for special focus on the, on the N E States alongwith the States not performing well. The
Department should take the initiative by actively monitoring the implementation of this programme in such States. The
Committee feels that local bodies, Gram Panchayats and community need to be actively involved, as their presence
would motivate the people at large to make use of the facilities available under this programme.
Action Taken
         The performance in the North Eastern States has been closely monitored. In order to enhance the eye care delivery
services, some of the steps taken are; (i) teams of Opthalmic Surgeons have been sent to these States for eye care
delivery services and surgery of cataract patients as and when required; 
(ii) Regional Institute of Ophtalmology was developed at Guwahati to cater to the eye care needs of the local
population, (iii) grant-in-aid has been sanctioned to NGOs for up-gradation/expansion of eye care delivery services; (iv)
funds were released for construction of eye wards and OTs, (v) Opthalmic equipments have been supplied for surgery,
(vi) the Opthalmic Surgeons are being trained in the modern surgery, (vii) rates for spectacles were enhanced so that the
poor may get the high quality glasses.
         In the Revised pattern of assistance, management support has been enhanced. Emphasis has also been laid to
involve the voluntary groups like Mahila Mandals and Gram Panchayats for motivating, organizing and transporting the
identified persons to Govt./VO fixed facilities and Primary Health Centres. Review meetings of the District Programme
Managers are being organized and the performance is closely monitored. All these steps are likely to enhance the
performance in the N.E. States.

         The Ministry has formulated a comprehensive National Mental Health Programme with an approved outlay of Rs.

XV.  NATIONAL AIDS CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
15.4  The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Department in the expansion of various components of the
programme having far reaching impact. The Committee is however, of the view that besides coordinating with Ministry
of Information and Broadcasting for Advertisements on dual use of condoms both for controlling AIDS and family
planning, the department should also take steps for ensuring the accessibility of condoms within the reach of people. For
example, truck drivers have been identified right from the beginning as a major source for spreading this disease. The
Committee recommends that the Department in coordination with the Department of Family Welfare take steps so that
condoms are made easily available at roadside dhabas, petrol pumps, check posts etc. The Committee would like to
emphasize that the Department will have to evolve an effective mechanism for constant monitoring of the above
mentioned initiatives.
Action Taken
         The following steps are being taken for ensuring the availability of condoms:----
            (1)     Mapping to identify high risk groups particularly truckers, female sex workers migrant labourers, IDUs
etc. has been intensified to cover all the states through State AIDS Control Societies/Municipal AIDS
Control Societies.
            (2)     Results of these mapping exercises are being intimated to 7 Social Marketing Organizations (SMOs)
included in the approved list of Department of Family Welfare and operating in various states. These
SMOs include HLL, Population Services of India (PSI), DKT India, Janani, Parivar Sewa Sansthan (PSS),
World Pharma, Indore, Dey’s Medical Stores, Kolkata etc.
            (3)     Social Marketing Organizations have been requested to prepare annual action plans for respective states in
consultation with SACS for promoting condoms amongst high risk groups.
            (4)     Free distribution of condoms has been intensified by SACS through NGOs for high risk groups who
cannot afford to pay the cost of condoms.
            (5)     Procurement of sufficient quantity of condoms for free distribution and social marketing is being done in
collaboration with the Department of Family Welfare.
            (6)     Social Marketing Organizations (SMOs) are establishing retail outlets for condoms in non conventional
areas such as Dhabas on the highways, halt points for truckers, automobile repair shops and petrol pumps.
            (7)     Trade Unions and Truckers Unions will be contacted for promoting usage of condom.
            (8)     Dual protection by condoms that is, protection of unwanted pregnancies and prevention of Sexually
Transmitted Infections (STIs) has been printed on each piece of condom for propagation of the message of
dual protection of condoms.
            (9)     Condom Vending Machines are being installed in High Risk Areas in collaboration with the Department
of Family Welfare.
Recommendations/Observations
15.5  The Committee was informed that HIV infection in India so far continues to remain concentrated among
marginalized groups including commercial sex workers, injecting drug users, truck drivers and migrant labourers. The
Committee feels that the trend of gradual spread of the infection from urban to rural areas and from the high risk to the
general population needs to be viewed seriously. To sensitize the general masses about HIV/AIDS, awareness
programme including publicity through print and media and also by dedicated NGOs is the need of the hour. The
Committee is of the view that in addition to routine publicity campaigns, inclusion of surrogate advertisements in films
in the form of dialogues will prove to be very effective in increasing awareness about AIDS in general public. Such

4th Report of Committee on Health & Family Welfare

programmes need to be made region-specific. The Committee is of the view that the Department should involve other
Departments like Department of Women and Child Development, Elementary and Secondary Education, Family
Welfare and also Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for having an effective publicity programme.
Action Taken
         The trend of gradual spread of HIV from urban to rural areas and from high risk to general population is being
monitored closely by annual sentinel surveillance in the country. A behavioral Surveillance Survey has been planned to
be conducted during the first quarter of the year 2005. Following steps are being taken for prevention and control of
HIV transmission:----
           (a)     For sensitization of general masses, awareness is being done through print, electronic
and folk media.
           (b)     At present there are 933 Target Intervention Projects engaged to provide services for the various high risk
groups across the country for counselling of high risk groups, early detection and treatment of STI/RTI,
promotion of condoms, counselling for behavioral change and referral of the needy patients of care and
support.
           (c)     A feature film has been made entitled “Phir Milenge” in collaboration with UNAIDS which conveys
surrogate messages on prevention and control of HIV/AIDS. Special advocacy workshops to sensitize the
media men responsible for production of films/serials with surrogate advertisements have been conducted
by NACO.
           (d)     The suggestions of the committee for surrogate ads in the form of dialogue will be included in the film
spots to be developed under the programme.
           (e)     The Department of Women and Child Development is being involved for expending the services for parent
to child transmission of HIV/AIDS.
           (f)      Department of Education, Nehru Yuva Kendras, Universities and Colleges are being
involved for creating AIDS awareness amongst school children, college students and out of school youth in
the villages.
           (g)     Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is being involved for providing adequate coverage on messages
related to HIV/AIDS for wider publicity.
XVIII. PUBLIC GRIEVANCES CELL
Recommendations/Observations
18.0  Besides a Public Grievances Cell in the Ministry, complaints pertaining to treatment of patients in three Central
Government Hospitals in Delhi are referred to the Grievances Redress at Cell in the Ministry. There is another
Grievances Redressal Cell functioning since 1997 where complaints received from all the States/UTs are sent to the
State authorities for necessary action. Directorate General of Health Services also has its separate Grievances cell.
Besides that, each Government Hospital has a separate Public Grievance Officer. However, general public, the main
beneficiaries of Government hospitals is not aware of such Grievance Redressal channels. The Committee would like to
emphasize that there is a need for giving wide publicity to the Public Grievance Cells set up at different places so that
public at large can avail of such a facility for redressal of their grievances. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Department should take appropriate action in this matter.
Action Taken
         As part of their Annual Action Plan the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances issues
advertisement in the newspapers for information of general public publicizing, inter-alia, the names, designation, office
address/phone/fax number and e-mail address of the Joint Secretary/Director of Grievances designated by the
Ministries/Departments as the contact Officer for redress of public grievances.
         The name, designation, room number, telephone number, etc. of the Director of Grievances of the Department of
Health, DGHS and CGHS have been displayed at the reception and in the IFC Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi.
         Similarly, names and address of Public Grievances Officers designated by the Central Government Hospitals are
also displayed at prominent places so that general public is aware of existence of such facility for redressal of their
grievances.

Recommendations/Observations
21.0  The Committee was informed that under the Health Sector Disaster Management, the Government is procuring a
self-contained container based mobile hospital, which can be transported through prime movers/aircraft to the disaster

site rendering immediate medical relief. The state-of-art unit would have operation theatres, post-operative intensive
care unit, laboratories, imaging facilities, tentage having capacity of 100 bed ward, kitchen and safe drinking water
facility. Ministry of Health & Family Welfare is in the process of procuring one such unit to be stationed at Dr. Ram
Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, at an estimated cost of about Rs. 20 crores. The MHA is also planning to procure

requires to be actively strengthened to provide adequate Health Sector Disaster Management preparedness in the
country.
Action Taken
         The scheme on Health Sector Disaster Preparedness and Management has the following objectives. Objectives :
           (1)   To strengthen and operationalize the control room and to establish networking with
National Operation Centres and the State Control Rooms.
           (2)   To provide emergency support functions
           (3)   To contribute to national disaster quick response mechanism. Components and actions taken:
           (4)   To strengthen and operationalise the control room and to establish networking with national operation
centers and the State Control Rooms.
         Creation of state of art facilities in the control rooms such as telecommunication networks, computer, internet and
Fax to facilitate timely collection, collation, analysis and dissemination of information for emergency support functions,
disaster quick response mechanisms and monitoring disaster management in 15 State Headquarters (including North
Eastern States). Establishment/strengthening of Headquarters control room in Dte.G.H.S. with above facilities.
Actions Taken
         Components of the Scheme has been circulated to all North Eastern States (including Sikkim) inviting proposals
for assistance under the scheme. Proposals have been received from the States of Tripura, Nagaland and Manipur for
strengthening of control room Hospitals would be equipped with portable CT Scan, portable X-ray, Ultrasound,
monitors, ECG with defibrillator and external pace maker, blood gas analyzer, ventilator etc. Consumable items like
medicines, POP, bandages, X-ray plates etc. would also be stockpiled exclusively for use in the disaster wards. The
strengthening of disaster beds would ensure state of art medical care to the victims of disasters.
2.      To provide emergency support functions.
         To augment the emergency support function without disturbing the normal functioning of the hospital, it has been
proposed under the Tenth Five Year Plan to strengthen disaster wards in Government institutions. Under this component
the existing disaster beds in the Hospitals would be equipped with portable CT Scan, portable X-ray, Ultrasound,
monitors, ECG with defibrillator and external pace maker, blood gas analyzer, ventilator etc. Consumable items like
medicines, POP, bandages, X-ray plates etc. would also be stockpiled exclusively for use in the disaster wards. The
strengthening of disaster beds would ensure state of art medical care to the victims of disasters.
Action Taken
         Components of the scheme has been circulated to all North Eastern States (including Sikkim) inviting proposals
for assistance under the scheme. Proposals have been received from the States of Tripura, Nagaland and Manipur for
strengthening of disaster wards which is under consideration. Other States have been reminded to send the proposal.
3.      To contribute to National Disaster quick response mechanism.
         The country has witnessed major disasters in the recent years. A major impediment for quick response mechanism
was non availability of dedicated secondary/tertiary level medical facilities near the disaster site. It has also been
observed that a large number of deaths could be prevented with such facilities. The experience of managing disaster on
a global context has established that container based, self contained mobile units having facilities for operation theatres,
pathology labs, imaging units and other support functions moved to the disaster site at short notice would augment the
quick response mechanism and save many preventable deaths. The High Powered Committee also has recommended
setting up of 5 to 6 units all over India. One such unit would be procured under the scheme during Tenth Five Year plan.
Actions Taken
         The concept of establishing a pre-fabricated, self contained, container based mobile hospital was crystallized in a
series of meetings held under the Chairmanship of Director General of Health Services. Technical specifications were
vetted by a team of experts. M/S Hospital Services Consultancy Corporation, a Government of India Enterprise has been
engaged as the procurement consultant for the above project.

III.    CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HEALTH SCHEME
Recommendations/Observations
3.2    The Committee was informed that a decision was taken by the Department to decentralize the work related to
reimbursement of medical claims of pensioners being handled by the CGHS by transferring the same to the parent
departments of the pensioners.
Recommendations/Observations
3.3    Accordingly, vide Department O.M. dated 14.10.03, the pensioner was given an option to seek settlement of
medical claims either from the Department from where he/she retired or from the Department of Health. In anticipation
of a positive response from majority of the pensioners, allocation in 
BE-2004-05, was kept at a much lower rate. The Committee, however, notes that in view of lack of positive response
from the beneficiaries, the decentralization scheme has been kept in abeyance since 12
th May, 2004.
Recommendations/Observations
3.4    The Committee fails to understand the non-acceptance of this initiative by majority of the pensioners. The
Committee feels that the idea of decentralizing the work relating to reimbursement of claims of pensioners to their
respective Departments from where they had retired is a welcome one. The Committee would like to have the feedback
from the Department regarding percentage of pensioners who had shown reluctance/non acceptance to this reported
move of the Department.

         The Decentralization process was initially circulated in four (4) CGHS-covered metropolitan cities viz., Delhi

beneficiaries of Central Government Health Scheme were required to fill up the option forms for indicating whether
they would like to get reimbursement from the office from which they retired or continue getting reimbursement from
the Central Government Scheme. The option forms that were received by the Central Government Scheme up to

Recommendations/Observations
2.2    The Committee notes that position of outlays approved during the first three years of the Tenth Plan vis-a-vis the

Recommendations/Observations
2.3    The Committee is in agreement with the Department’s contention that approved plan outlay of 
Rs. 4900 crores for the first three years of Tenth Plan leaves a disproportionately high balance of 
Rs. 5352 crores for the remaining two years of the plan period. The Committee was informed that against the projected
demand of Rs. 2547.50 crores for 2004-05 by the Department, allocation of only Rs. 1800.00 crores will adversely
affect the implementation of important programmes and functioning of research and medical institutions. The
Committee observes with concern that amongst the major programmes/institutions to be adversely affected, the
following fall-out will be very critical
            —     NACP-II Project (Rs. 1941.91 crore) had to be extended by two years up to 2006-07 because of the
consistently low level of outlays approved since 1999-2000, which is seriously affecting the credibility of
Government before bilateral/multilateral funding agencies.
            —     Initiative of introducing Anti-retroviral Treatment to one lakh patients of high prevalence States requiring a
provision of Rs. 100 crores would suffer.
            —     Approved outlay for Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme will cover 80-90 districts only against
proposed 130-140 districts.
            —     Apex Trauma Centre (Rs. 132.82 crore - Expenditure of Rs. 35.23 crore already incurred at AIIMS, New
Delhi.
            —     ICMR will not be able to fund any new project for the second consecutive year.
         Viewing this with serious concern, the Committee would like to reiterate its earlier observation made at the time of
consideration of Demands for Grants, 2003-04 of the Department that priority areas such as public health should be
spared from the cuts imposed by the Planning Commission/Ministry of Finance.
2.4    The Committee feels that the Department has a strong case for asking for enhancement in the Plan outlay
specifically for 2004-05 by Rs. 747.50 crore taking the total to Rs. 2547.50 crores in 2004-05, the amount asked by
them at the time of regular budget. Keeping in view the need for having an enhanced allocation for proper
implementation of its various programmes and efficient functioning of its premier institutions, the Committee
recommends that the allocation for the Department needs to be enhanced appropriately.

time of regular budget a demand of Rs. 2547.50 crores was projected for the Annual Plan, 2004-05 but the outlay was
kept at the level of interim budget i.e. at Rs. 1800 crores leaving a shortfall of Rs.747.50 crores. Planning Commission
has now subsequently allocated an outlay of Rs.408.00 crores for 2004-05 raised in the form of Supplementary Grant

2. National TB Control Programme 15

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee notes that with an additional grant of Rs. 408 crores in the form of Supplementary Grants for
2004-05, the gap in the requirement and allocation of funds for some major programmes has been bridged to some
extent. However, a shortfall of Rs. 339.50 crores is still left from the proposed outlay of Rs. 2547.50 crores. The

that such important programmes of public health should be allocated sufficient funds to face the challenges in health
care system. Further the submission of the Department that even after this additional allocation, there is a
disproportionately high balance of Rs. 4944 crores for the remaining two years of the Tenth plan, is worth considering
and needs serious attention of the Government. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation for allocation
of adequate funds to the Department for the remaining two years of the Tenth plan.
Recommendations/Observations
2.5    The Committee would, however, like to point out that while advocating higher allocation to meet the requirement
of different programmes etc. in 2004-05, the Department should also keep in mind the funds allocated to Ninth Plan

         The total utilization during Ninth Plan was Rs. 4997.73 crores, after including the expenditure incurred by
Ministry of Urban Development on capital works, which covered in the approved outlay of Rs. 5118.19 crores (98 per

         Even after including the reported additional expenditure incurred by the Ministry of Urban Development the total

the Finance Ministry. The Committee is of the view that the Department should not leave the balance unspent and use it
judiciously in a time-bound manner.
Recommendations/Observations

Rs. 5118.19 crores. The first two years of Tenth Plan do not indicate any improvement so far as utilisation of allocated
funds is concerned. Plan allocation of Rs. 1550.00 crores in 2002-03 had to be reduced to Rs. 1375.00 crores at the RE

that the year 2004-05 being the third year of Tenth Plan is the right stage for taking a mid-term appraisal of all the
programmes/institutions of the Department, specially those not performing well and taking remedial steps wherever
required.

         While advocating higher allocation of funds for the vital sector of health, the Committee views with serious
concern the Department’s inability to fully utilise the allocated funds. The Committee feels that only constant

III.    CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HEALTH SCHEME
Recommendations/Observations
3.5    Last year, the Committee was informed that a Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr. R.K. Srivastava, Addl.
Director General in the Directorate General of Health Services had been constituted to prepare the combined drugs
formulary of the CGHS and MSO and its report was being examined then. The Committee was given to understand that
once the new drugs formulary was formally notified, the procurement of drugs for the CGHS would be based on time.
The Committee is constrained to observe that one year has passed and the recommendations of the Committee on drugs
formulary are still under the consideration of the Department. It seems that the Department has no time bound action
plan for notification of the drugs formulary. The Committee feels that notification of the new Drugs formulary would
lead to quality control of drugs being provided through CGHS dispensaries. The Committee enjoins upon the
Department to get all the formalities completed for notification of drugs formulary.
Action Taken
         On the basis of the recommendations of a Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr. R.K. Shrivastava, Addl. DG.
DGHS, the combined formulary of CGHS/MSO in respect of Proprietary Medicines has been prepared and the process
of fixation of rates of formulary are in progress.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee expresses its deep sense of concern over the undue delay being taken in the issuing of notification
on the drugs formulary. The Committee’s observation on this issue do not seem to have made any significant impact.
Process of fixation of rates of formulary still remains to be completed. The Committee reiterates that the Departments
should get completed this process without any further delay.
Recommendations/Observations
3.6    The Committee in its 135th Report had strongly advocated the need for restoring the earlier two-shift system in
CGHS dispensaries which was more convenient for the beneficiaries. The Department has justified the single shift
working of CGHS dispensaries due to majority of CGHS employees commuting daily from long distances. The
Committee was given to understand that double shift system is practically impossible for such employees. The
Committee expresses its dissatisfaction about the justification given by the Department for having a single shift system
for the dispensaries. The Committee further recommends that the Department should first make an assessment about the
requirement of staff for running CGHS dispensaries in double shift. Based on that, the Department may take steps to
have additional workforce for the CGHS dispensaries.
Action Taken
         Assessment about the requirement of staff for running Central Government Health Scheme dispensaries in double
shift is being calculated and will be submitted in due course.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee has been commenting on the need for restoring the double shift system for the CGHS dispensaries
prevalent some years ago. The Committee has observed that the Department is not inclined to revert back to the earlier
system and has been advancing unconvincing reasons therefor. The Committee would like to point out that under the
double shift system also, working hours would remain the same. If the CGHS employees residing nearest to a particular
dispensary are posted there, to the extent possible, chances of undue hardship to the CGHS employees will also stand
eliminated. In this way, CGHS beneficiaries will be in a position to obtain the maximum benefit of medical facilities
available at CGHS dispensaries, the purpose for which they have been set up.

VI.    ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES, (AIIMS) NEW DELHI
Recommendations/Observations
6.2    The Committee is deeply anguished to observe that although considerable time has elapsed the Trauma Centre is
yet to be established. The Committee observes that the revised EFC for Trauma centre is yet to be approved. Rs. 17.65
crores are proposed to be utilized for the construction of Trauma Centre in 2004-05. Thereafter, approximately Rs.
47.05 crore would be required for procurement of equipment. The Committee apprehends that due to procedural
formalities, formal approval of revised EFC may take some more time, which would result in cost escalation in the
initial proposed amount for setting up of Trauma Centre. The Committee is of the strong view, that the Department in
coordination with the AIIMS should get all the procedural formalities expedited so that the Trauma Centre becomes
functional at the earliest.

         A meeting of the Expenditure Finance Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Expenditure) was held on
17.9.2004 to consider the proposal of the Department of Health on the revised cost estimates for setting up of an Apex
Trauma Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi. The draft Cabinet Note for establishment of
Trauma Centre was circulated to the appraising agencies i.e. Ministry of Finance, Planning Commission, etc. Comments
have been obtained and of appraising Agencies is in the process of finalization. The Project Implementation Committee
has been set up by the Institute to monitor the project.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee observes that not much progress has been made in the establishment of Trauma Center at AIIMS.
Procedural formalities are yet to be completed. An amount of 
Rs. 17.65 crores proposed to be utilized for the construction of Trauma Center in 2004-05 would thus remain unutilized
at the end of the year. The Committee reiterates that the Department should get all the procedural formalities completed
at the earliest so that construction of this over-delayed Center finally begins in 2005-06. Otherwise, the estimated cost of
the Project would keep on increasing and the public would also continue to remain deprived of the medical facilities to
be made available at the Trauma Center.

VII.  VACANCY POSITION IN CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS/ INSTITUTIONS /
         AUTONOMOUS ORGANISATIONS
Recommendations/Observations
7.3    The Committee was informed that at present there are 545 vacancies in Central Health Services in various Central
Government Hospitals like Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. RML Hospital, LHMC, JIPMER and other important institutions
out of which 222 are specialists. In addition, medical officers/specialists and scientists in various
institutions/autonomous organizations like AIIMS, PGIMER, NIMHANS and ICMR are also vacant. Large numbers of
vacancies of doctors, nurses and paramedics have adversely affected the services provided to the common man. In
addition, there has also not been any increase in manpower particularly in the technical cadre commensurate with the
increase in patient load over the years.
7.4    The Committee takes a serious view of this position. The Committee was given to understand that these posts were
lying vacant for a considerable time. The Committee notes that the Department has been repeatedly pleading for
exempting technical posts under it from the operation of Department of Personnel and Training orders regarding
reduction in staff and abolition of vacancies, but with no success. The Committee is of the view that direct recruitment
at various levels and filling of vacancies in the health institutions is vital in the interest of public health. Department of
Personnel instructions should not be made applicable in the case of technical posts. The Committee therefore, strongly
recommends that the Department should approach the Department of Personnel, once again, for exemption, if necessary
at the highest level so that continuing vacancies in a large number of operational posts of doctors, nurses, para-medical
and other supporting staff are filled up without any further delay.
Action Taken

VIII.NATIONAL VECTOR BORNE DISEASE CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
8.8    The Committee strongly recommends that the Department should carry out an assessment of the weak areas and
identify the constraints/problems being faced by the State Governments and other implementing agencies in the
implementation of the Programme and take remedial measures accordingly. The Department should evolve a monitoring
mechanism where under reports furnished by the state Governments. should not remain the only feed-back. The
Committee strongly feels that regular monitoring by periodic inspections including random surveys without any prior
notice will help in achieving the targeted goals under this programme.
Action Taken
         Monitoring under the programme is being done routinely through the reports received from the States and
necessary feedback on improving the situation of malaria is being conveyed to States on regular basis. Programme
Officers from the Directorate of NVBCP, Regional Offices for Health and Family Welfare, Government of India,
Malaria Research Centre, and other ICMR institutions are separately being deputed to states for review of the malaria
situation.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee’s attention has been drawn by the high incidence of malaria deaths in the country. The Committee
has observed that overall national figures of death cases continue to be high, with Orissa and West Bengal reporting the
maximum cases as per the figures pertaining to the period 1999-2003. The Committee has been given to understand that
both these States are being provided additional financial assistance for malaria control. The most affected districts have
been included for additional support under the Global Fund for AIDS, TB and Malaria. The Committee reiterates that
the Department should carry out an assessment of the weak areas and identify the constraints/ problems being faced by
the implementing agencies in malaria control. The Committee would also emphasise that random surveys/surprise
inspections need to be made by Central/State level teams.

Recommendations/Observations

9.3    The Committee notes that the annual incidence of Japanese Encephalitis in the country has declined since 1949
(3428 cases/680 deaths) and during 2002, only 1765 cases and 466 deaths were reported. There being no specific
treatment for JE, anticipatory preparations need to be made for timely availability of medicines, equipment trained
medical/para-medical personnel. The Committee was informed that due to availability of limited funds, cash assistance
of only Rs. 56 lakhs could be provided in training and IEC activities in the twelve JE affected States during 2003-04.
9.4    The Committee strongly feels that in view of number of reported cases of JE and deaths in highly endemic States,
additional funds need to be provided for taking required preventive measures of training and IEC activities in view of
there being no specific treatment for JE. The Committee therefore recommends that additional funds be provided in this
programme at the RE stage. The Department should also take the initiative in active coordination with the concerned
State Governments. for making an assessment of endemic districts so that preventive measures can be taken to avoid
outbreaks as reported on A.P and U.P in 2003.
Action Taken
         For Japanese Encephalitis, no provision available as Cash Grant in B.E. 2004. As per observation of the
Committee cash grant proposed will be included in the Annual Plan.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee expresses its dissatisfaction with the casual response of the Department to its specific
recommendation for providing cash grants to highly endemic States for IEC activities. The Committee finds that no
initiative has been taken by the Department to its suggestion for making a provision at the RE stage in 2003-04. The
Department has chosen not to react to Committee’s emphasis on having an assessment done of highly endemic districts
for taking preventive measures to avoid recurrence of outbreaks of cases of JE in Andhra Pradesh and U.P. Reiterating
its observation, the Committee hopes that the Department would act on its suggestion.

136.27 lakhs as Grant-in-aid in 2002-03, expenditure was only Rs. 76.78 lakhs. Position remains the same during 2003-

XIV.NATIONAL MENTAL HELATH PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
14.3  The Committee notes that an ambitious National Mental Health Programme with an approved outlay of Rs. 190
crores is proposed to be launched in the Tenth Plan. The Committee is of the view that the Department will have to take
specific steps for expansion of this programme in the maximum number of districts in the country to achieve the targets
set out in the Tenth Plan. The Committee is not aware whether any survey has been conducted so far with regard to
prevalence of mental health problems in different states of the country. The Committee is of the view that in order to
have effective implementation and maximum coverage; programme should first be extended to those districts where
such cases have been noticed more as compared to other areas.
Action Taken
         On the direction of Supreme Court of India in the Erwadi case, Chief Secretaries of all the States have got
conducted a need based survey about the mentally ill patients and the facilities available. It is on this basis that the
State/UTs were requested, during the launch workshop on National Mental Health Programme held in October, 2003 by
Central Government, to identify specific districts, psychiatric units and mental hospitals which require to be included in
the programme for funding. On the basis of this criteria, the State Governments have submitted proposals which are
under examination. It is felt that at the end of Tenth Plan, the National Mental Health Programme will have a maximum
coverage of districts in the country and thus improve the mental health care.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee is of the view that in order to utilise the approved outlay of Rs. 190/- crores to implement the
National Mental Health Programme during the Tenth Plan, necessary steps may be taken urgently on priority basis to
identify the districts so as to increase the coverage to 100 districts as planned. The Committee is of the opinion that
unless the districts are identified urgently the utilization of funds may not be achieved during the Tenth Plan.
XVI.NATIONAL CANCER CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendations/Observations
16.3  Plan allocation for National Cancer Control for 2004-05 is Rs. 53.00 crore. The Committee notes that during 2003-
04 plan allocation of Rs.49.00 crore had to be reduced to Rs.30.00 crore. The Committee feels that in view of cancer
becoming a major health programme in the country, concerted efforts need to be made by the Department for optimum
and judicious utilisation of allocated funds for the programme. The Department should also make an assessment of the
facilities available for treatment of Cancer in the country and take effective step for providing such facilities in areas not
covered/under-covered so far.

         All out efforts will be made by the Programme Division to utilize the grant amount of Rs.53.00 crores allocated

schemes will be circulated among the States/UTs and the RCCs asking them to send proposals and as soon as the
proposals are received, the same will be evaluated and sanctioned on merit.
         The earlier schemes of Oncology Development (only equipment grant) and Cobalt grant for Govt. Hospitals
(restricted to Rs. 1.5 crores) were not attractive as it required investment from State Governments. Under the revised
scheme upto Rs.3 crores can be allocated for comprehensive development of Government Medical College Hospitals
and Government Hospitals. With these modifications better responses from State Governments are expected. While

         In order to utilise the allocated funds for the National Cancer Control Programme, the Committee feels that the

with such equipment on priority basis so that they may function properly.
XX.  SUPPLY OF EQUIPMENT TO DISTRICT HOSPITALS
Recommendations/Observations
20.1  At present, there is no specific scheme/programme with the Department of Health for providing equipment support
to District Hospitals, although the facilities at district level are augmented under various diseases control programmes.
During the Ninth Plan on a pilot basis, financial assistance upto Rs. 1.5 crores was provided to the State Govts./UTs as
assistance for Capacity Building which included the following:-
           (a)    Upgradation and strengthening of EMERGENCY Services in State Government Hospitals located on
National Highways.
           (b)   Hospitals Waste Management.
           (c)    Strengthening of Diagnostic Facilities in select Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals.
20.2  However, during the Tenth Plan, only first two schemes at (a) and (b) could be taken up. With the limited plan
allocation, the scheme for strengthening of diagnostic facilities had to be dropped for want of funds. The Committee is
of the view that this is an area where additional resources and strengthening of medical facilities at the district level
would go a long way in improving the provisions of secondary health care to the public. The Department should initiate
an exercise of assessing the needs/status of infrastructure available at Govt. medical Colleges and hospitals and start
with providing relief to those institutions which are in a very bad shape.
Action Taken
         A need was felt in the Central Government to strengthen the existing diagnostic facilities in Government Medical
Colleges and Hospitals to enable them to provide better health care facilities as well as cope with increased rush of
patients and tide over with the problem of obsolescence of equipments.
         Accordingly, during the Ninth Five Year Plan period under the Capacity Building Project, three different projects
were implemented on a pilot basis viz.
           (1)   Upgradation and strengthening of EMERGENCY services in State Government Hospitals located on
National Highways.
           (2)   Hospital Waste Management.
           (3)   Strengthening of Diagnostic facilities in select Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals.
         However, during the Tenth Five Year Plan, of the above three projects, the schemes mentioned at (1) and (3) were
continued with an outlay of Rs. 110 crores and were proposed to be implemented as Centrally Sponsored Schemes
under New Initiatives. Though the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was given “In-Principle” approval by the
Planning Commission for implementing the Scheme on strengthening of diagnostic facilities with an enhanced quantum
of financial assistance from Rs. l.5 crores to Rs. 5 crores for each college and despite a lot of demand from various State
Governments/Union Territories, this scheme had to be discontinued in view of the fact that the total outlay of Rs. 110
crores under New Initiatives was found inadequate to cater to the prevailing demand from various Government medical
colleges and hospitals.
         Since this scheme was discontinued only for want of resources, provisioning of additional resources as suggested
in the report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee would certainly help in reviving 
this scheme for Strengthening of Diagnostic Facilities in select Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals.
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee feels that the Department should not do injustice to the scheme by discontinuing it for want of
adequate funds to cater to the prevailing demands from various Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals. The
Committee feels that a suitable procedure in allocating the available resources in a just, equitable and judicious manner
may be devised. The recommendation of the Committee that the Department should initiate an exercise of assessing the
needs/status of infrastructure available at Govt. Medical Colleges and hospitals and start with providing relief to those

4th Report of Committee on Health & Family Welfare
file:///D/health_family/4threport.htm[29-06-2016 14:38:53]
institutions which are in a very bad shape, has not been taken in right perspective. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Scheme of Strengthening of Diagnostic facilities in selected Government Medical Colleges and
Hospitals should be revived from the ensuing financial year 2005-2006 and the available resources may be provided to
those institutions which are in a very bad shape and deficient in diagnostic facilities after assessing their requirements
and status.
XXII.CONTRIBUTION FROM MPLAD FUND
Recommendations/Observations
22.0  The Committee observes that shortage of funds is one of the factors responsible for lack of required health services
for the common people. The Committee strongly feels that one of the initiatives that can go a long way in improving
health sector facilities throughout the country is a stipulation that 25 percent of the funds allocated under MPLAD
should be reserved for projects in the health sector. This would actively involve the MPs in health related issues in their
respective constituencies as well help in upgradation of health infrastructure in their areas.
Action Taken                                                                                                                               
         NIL
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
         The Committee made the above recommendation with the hope that the Department would approach the
concerned Ministry in the Govt. i.e. the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation so that necessary changes
in the guidelines to spend the MPLAD funds are placed before the respective Parliamentary Committees on MPLAD in
Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. However, the Department has done nothing in this regard. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department should take suitable action in this regard.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT ARE STILL AWAITED
XVII. NATIONAL ILLNESS ASSISTANCE FUND
Recommendations/Observations
17.2  The Committee notes that during 2003-04, financial assistance of Rs. 78.54 lakh was granted to patients. Besides
that assistance was also provided to NIMHANS, Bangalore, AIIMS, Delhi, CNCI Kolkata, JIPMER Pondicherry and
Illness assistance Fund Society Lakshadweep for maintaining their revolving fund. The Committee notes that thirteen
States/UTs were released financial assistance under the society. The Committee was given to understand that all the
States are not maintaining such a fund. The Committee feels that the Department should pursue with the States not
covered so far to setup such a fund.
Action Taken
         At present, following States/UTs are maintaining State Illness Fund with a view to provide an assistance up to Rs.
1.5 lakhs in an individual case to the patients Below Poverty Line (BPL), suffering from life threatening diseases and
taking treatment in a Government hospital, viz., (i) Karnataka  (ii) Madhya Pradesh (iii) Tripura (iv) Andhra Pradesh (v)
Tamil Nadu (vi) Himachal Pradesh (vii) Jammu & Kashmir (viii) Maharashtra (ix) West Bengal (x) Kerala (xi)
Mizoram (xii) Rajasthan (xiii) Goa 
(xiv) Gujarat (xv) Sikkim (xvi) Bihar (xvii) Chhattisgarh (xviii) Jharkhand (xix) Uttaranchal (xx) NCT of Delhi and
(xxi) Pondicherry. The State/UT level funds could also seek contributions/donations from private charity/industry for
which income tax exemption is given. The Central Government releases grant in aid to the extent of Rs. 50 per cent of
the contribution made by a State, subject to maximum of  Rs. 5 crores to States with larger number and percentage of
population Below Poverty Line and  Rs. 2 crores to other States/UTs with legislatures, in a year.
         Some States (viz. Assam, Haryana, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Orissa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and
Nagaland) are reluctant to set up such a fund. Despite repeated requests and follow up action, these States have not
responded. A possible reason could be the current sharing pattern under the scheme of l/3
rd Central contribution to the
2/3rd contribution made by the State concerned. A proposal for modifying the scheme so that the sharing of
contributions is 50:50 between Central Government and State Government is, therefore, being moved for consideration.
XIX.SETTING UP OF MEDICAL GRANTS COMMISSION
Recommendations/Observations
19.0  The Committee notes that setting up of Medical Grants Commission has been provided in the National Health
Policy, 2002. Apart from its role in coordination in the field of Education and Health Science, it is also envisaged that
the Medical Grants Commission would fund the upgradation of the infrastructure of the existing Government. Medical
and Dental colleges so as to ensure an improved standard of medical education. The Committee notes that in BE 2004-
05 (plan), only a token provision of Rs. 1.00 crore has been made. The Committee feels that this is a proposal which
needs to be actively supported in the overall interest of health sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
adequate provision for this purpose may be made at the RE stage.
Action Taken
         Medical Grants Commission has been proposed to act as a funding agency through which the Government can
provide continuous financial assistance to various medical colleges and its attached hospitals under the Government
sector. Planning Commission has asked the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to examine the possibility of this
scheme being merged with any other scheme of similar nature.
         In this connection, considering the fact that upgradation of primary health in the backward area of the country
would require strong manpower support which in turn depends on the quality of medical education being imparted by
the Government medical colleges, it has been felt that funding for the Medical Grants Commission could be channelized
through the fund allocation to be made to the Department of Family Welfare under Rural Health Scheme. The details
are in the process of being worked out.
